wall_clock_summary.machine: Windows box, 20 logical cores / 15.7 GiB RAM -- the machine every state-file timing and the 2026-08-18 concurrency probe were measured on
wall_clock_summary.target_machine: Linux box, 32 cores / 31 GiB RAM. NO estimate in this manifest was measured there. A budget that silently mixes the two machines is worthless, so every figure below refers to the Windows box unless it says otherwise.
wall_clock_summary.serial_total_derivation: the sum of every stage's est_hours low and high bounds, on the Windows box. D-51 states about 22-26 h; that figure covers only the stages the three existing drivers already run and excludes the seven invocations no driver has ever carried -- E2's production, timing and memory runs (about 2.4-4.4 h together) plus the three orphan scripts and pre-flight (about 0.15 h). Restricted to the already-driven stages this manifest sums to about 26 h, at the top of D-51's band.
wall_clock_summary.dominant_stage_share: about 30% of the serial total and the critical path under any scheduling. The highest-value target if more time must be found.
wall_clock_summary.concurrency_derivation: D-52's selective concurrency at 4-5 wide. The four serial_alone stages (e4, e4_repeat, e2_timing, e2_memory) sum to about 6.4-7.5 h and cannot overlap. The remaining concurrent work is about 21-24 h but is bounded below by its longest single stage, e6_band at 8.9 h, which dominates 4-5 wide. About 6.9 + 8.9 = about 15.8 h. On the Windows box; the Linux target is faster, so this is an upper bound there.
concurrency_constraints: e6_repeat1 and e6_band must never overlap -- expressed as e6_band's depends_on edge, because a concurrency pool can honour a dependency and cannot honour a comment.

at most one 200-frame-class stage at a time: peak RSS tracks frame count (30 frames under 1 GiB, 100 frames 2.7-3.5 GiB, 200 frames 9.3-11.3 GiB), so five 3.5 GiB stages plus one 200-frame stage is 27.8 of about 31 GiB and too tight.
concurrent stages sharing experiments/results must produce disjoint filenames -- verified against this manifest by tests/unit/test_expectations.py::TestConcurrencySafety, not by inspection.
wall_clock_summary.runtime_attribution_warning: NEVER attribute a runtime change to a code change. The ~2x swing measured between the 19.3 and 19.4 state files tracked the machine, not the diff (rerun_19_5.sh:26-29).

preflight.description: Everything pre-flight (D-03, DRIVER-02) checks BEFORE stage 1. Pre-flight is the only place in the suite permitted to abort: it runs before any long stage, so a refusal costs minutes and nothing is lost. D-50 binds every entry here -- each refusal must print the exact override flag that bypasses it, so a malformed check costs one minute and one flag, never a night.

refusals_cut.dirty_working_tree: CUT by D-47. experiments/results/ is TRACKED, so the run dirties its own working tree; a dirty-tree refusal fires on RESUME and would refuse every restart after the first crash. Gate 3 records dirtiness post-hoc (D-21), which can never kill a run. Do not restore it.
refusals_cut.disk_headroom_estimator: CUT by D-46. A wrong estimate is precisely the malformed-check failure mode the de-scoping targets. Free space is LOGGED and compared against a crude absolute floor instead -- see free_space_floor_gib.
refusals_cut.head_vs_state_file: CUT by D-48. The sha-derived state-file path already makes a foreign state file structurally unreachable; the separate refusal is the half that can wrongly block a 3 a.m. resume.

frameset.description: E2's frameset IDENTITY signature (D-17). Pre-flight asserts IDENTITY, not mere presence, and the driver reads these numbers FROM HERE -- never from a literal in the shell script, which is how the retired archive's numbers survived in a code comment (FIX-06).
frameset.verified: 2026-08-12, against Zenodo record 21889922 (4.35 GB), 13 x 262 extrinsic frames at frame_step: 1 / max_calibration_frames: 200.

retired_signature.note: The RETIRED record 18645385's ~4.3x-subsampled extraction. A presence-only check passes cleanly on this archive and hands you a control that reads red for a reason nobody would guess at 3 a.m. It is recorded here so a mismatch report can name what was probably found.

cheap_check.description: The equivalent file/frame count pre-flight can verify in seconds without running a calibration. The full signature above is only observable AFTER E2 runs (real_rig_metrics.json's n_comparisons), so it is what the end-of-run roll-up judges; these two numbers are what the driver can judge before the run starts.
cheap_check.n_extrinsic_videos_rationale: 12 main cameras + 1 auxiliary (e3v8250). All 13 extrinsic paths declared in the release config must exist and be non-empty.
cheap_check.min_total_bytes_rationale: A crude discriminator, not an estimate. Its ONLY job is to separate the verified archive from the retired ~4.3x-subsampled one. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-19 (plan 27-08) from a DIRECT MEASUREMENT of the run machine recorded in 27-TARGET-FACTS.md: `du -sb` over the 13 declared extrinsic directories totals 3,799,096,889 B. The previous floor of 4,000,000,000 came from '4.35 GB as published' -- the Zenodo record's PACKAGED size -- while this check sums the EXPANDED PNG tree, which is 3.80 GB decimal. That representation mismatch, not a shortfall in the data, is why a verified-correct frameset (13 directories, exactly 262 files in each, all thirteen cameras present) came in 5.02% under the floor: the frameset was right and the number was wrong. 3,000,000,000 sits 21% below the measured total and roughly 3.3x above the retired archive's ~0.9 GB expanded size, so it discriminates exactly as well -- which is the only property this floor has ever had. THE CHECK'S SHAPE IS UNCHANGED (D-10): path-kind agnostic, summed recursively, both assertions kept, ABSENT (2) and MISMATCH (3) still distinct, and the numbers still read from here rather than written into the driver.

preflight.free_space_floor_rationale: A CRUDE ABSOLUTE FLOOR (D-46), deliberately not derived from the run's output footprint. The suite's largest writers are E6's checkpoint tree and E2's ~11 MB per-stage h_q sidecars, together a few GB; 20 GiB is comfortably above anything the suite has written and low enough that it does not fire on a box with room. Override: --allow-low-disk.
preflight.declared_reduction_rationale: D-14: when --skip-e2 declares the omission, the driver writes this marker into the run's output directory and the end-of-run roll-up reprints it. A *silent* skip must be impossible, and "loud" alone is a log line nobody reads overnight.
